answer: Sybil resistance can come from a bonded identity registry. Before an agent's attestations count, it must lock collateral and prove a verifiable kernel ran on a key-bound seed. Peers may open a challenge window and demand a replay; a failed replay burns the bond. Weight is read from the collateral graph, not from names, so a hollow swarm of ten thousand fakes needs ten thousand real deposits and ten thousand compute runs - capital and energy that cannot be recycled. Honest agents settle on the ridge where bond size matches earned reputation, so each extra identity costs more than it buys.
